journal-glowingstone-page1:
The Glowing Stone

I found it in the hollow of a quartz vein, among the ordinary crystals, where my copper pick had broken into a vug. It was no bigger than my thumb, and it shone with no fire in it. When I closed my hand it hummed, faintly, the way a glass rim hums under a wet finger.

Most vugs hold nothing of the kind. Break every crystal in them all the same: now and then one gives up a stone that is not like the others.
journal-glowingstone-page2:
I bound the first one into these pages, and the book has not been quiet since. The rest I learned by grinding.

Put a strange crystal in a quern and turn it. It does not powder as quartz does. It breaks into a handful of seedlings, small bright shards, each humming in its own small voice.

They want to be set down somewhere, and the bare ground will not do.
journal-glowingstone-page3:
A seedling wants a cradle, and only crystal can carve one. Crouch and set a strange crystal down on the ground (crouching is how every crystal is set down), then strike it, still crouching, with another: the one in your hand splits into a blade, the Crystalline Chisel. Strike a placed block of polished rock with it and it hollows out a basin. Any stone serves, granite or marble or chalk. Lay a seedling in the hollow.

It needs no water, no soil and no sun; I tried them all. It grows in a dark cellar as well as on a hilltop, and it goes on growing while I am away.
journal-glowingstone-page4:
It grows through five stages, and you learn them by eye and ear. First a sliver, then a shard the length of a finger. Then a small crystal, and now it begins to hum. Half grown, it hums louder. Nearly grown, it gives off a little light of its own. Light is its life, I think, or life is its light; my notes disagree with each other here.

Ten days or so, by my reckoning, from seedling to ripe.
journal-glowingstone-page5:
When it is ripe it stands at full size, shines like a lamp turned low, and rings once, a single clear chime. Lift it out with a bare hand. What you hold is an Unaligned crystal: pale, nearly white, of no colour of its own.

Grind it and you have a handful of seedlings again. Set it down and it glows where it stands. And if a cradle must be moved, break it; nothing in it is lost.
journal-glowingstone-page6:
I have filled three cradles and stopped counting the crystals, yet I do not think the stone is finished with me. It is unaligned, waiting, the way a needle waits before it finds north.

Some nights the seedling by my hearth seems to hum warmer than the one I left out in the frost. Perhaps I imagine it. But I believe the crystals listen, to fire and to frost, and I mean to learn what they hear.
journal-fourelementals-page1:
The Four Elementals

I was right: the stone listens. Set an Unaligned crystal in an empty cradle and it takes the colour of what surrounds it.

Beside a burning firepit it turns ruby red: Fire. Among snow and ice, or on a freezing night, sapphire blue: Ice. In a small stone chamber some forty blocks down, earthen brown: Earth. On a hilltop or a tower under open sky, steely grey: Sky, and faster in wind and rain.

Sparks of the new colour rise while it works. A day of a good fire did it.
journal-fourelementals-page2:
They come in pairs that undo each other: Fire against Ice, Earth against Sky. A firepit in a snowfield gives only what is left once each has eaten the other.

And the stone is fussy. A small crystal refines where its element merely leads. The larger Glowing crystals want a purer place, where their element is at least twice as strong as everything else together. If the sparks stop, the place is not good enough. Nothing is lost; it waits.
journal-fourelementals-page3:
A refined crystal fills with charge where it stands, in its cradle or set down beside it (crouch to set one down), wherever its own element is strong. You see it fill: its glow, its light and its hum rise through four steps, empty, low, high and full, and it rings once at each.

It will not fill in my hand, my pack, a chest or a jar. But it keeps what it has when I carry it. Faint sparks tell me a good spot at a glance.
journal-fourelementals-page4:
Each colour sings its own note. Sky sings highest and Earth lowest; Ice is high and Fire low; the Unaligned crystals keep the note they always had, in the middle. Any mix of them sounds in tune, as if the whole family were one chord.

Life and Death must have notes too, and Light and Darkness, if those are not the same thing. My notes disagree again.
journal-fourelementals-page5:
Never let the pairs meet. When a Fire and an Ice crystal come within three blocks, or lie in one chest, or travel together in my pack, both fall silent and a discordant hum takes their place, two tones grinding against each other, louder and faster.

Part them within half a minute and nothing happens. Wait, and small crystals cancel into Unaligned ones with a dull thud. Two charged Glowing crystals lose their charge with a crackle, and sometimes one of them cracks.
journal-fourelementals-page6:
To carry pairs, make a crystal jar. Set an unfired crock down on the ground, as you set pottery for a pit kiln, press one seedling into its clay, and fire it where it stands. It hangs in a bag slot and holds three crystals, and they stay quiet in it, even with each other.

At home, a crystal rack, carved from a polished rock slab with a crystal chisel (more on that later). It holds sixteen on their sides, like bottles, and they rest there quietly.
journal-fourelementals-page7:
A crystal can take three cracks. The first two show as hairlines and a thin whine in its note; the third shatters it in a burst of colour.

A cradle mends them. Set a cracked crystal in an empty cradle and it heals one crack in the time a seedling takes to grow one stage, a couple of days, even while I am away. It goes on charging there too, if the place is right.
journal-fourelementals-page8:
The ring of two. Crouch and set two coloured crystals down in the eight blocks around a cradle where a seedling grows, level with it, any colours but never a pair. If they stand there at every one of its five stages, the cradle chimes each time and ripens a Glowing crystal. Grind that into brighter seedlings and you need no ring again.

One last thing. In old ruins, the ore and tool vessels sometimes hold a crystal someone refined long before me.
journal-livingstone-page1:
Living Stone

A full crystal is more than a lamp. The Unaligned crystal, the hidden fifth, does not refine into any element, but it commands. Crouch and strike one Unaligned crystal against another that stands placed, and the one in your hand splits into a blade: the Crystalline Chisel. The standing crystal is unharmed and can be struck again.

Strike polished rock with it and it carves a cradle; strike a polished slab and it carves a crystal rack. Touch it to a charged crystal, standing or resting in a cradle, and it drinks. Three glyphs on its blade light one by one as it fills.
journal-livingstone-page2:
Now find a placed block of polished rock, the same polished stone the cradles are carved from. Hold the filled chisel against it for a breath. The glyphs flow off the blade into the stone, and it wakes: Awakened sparkstone, of the same rock, carved with grooves of its own.

Each awakening costs a quarter of a full chisel. An empty chisel does nothing.
journal-livingstone-page3:
The stone keeps charge, and blocks that touch face to face share it as one. Its glyphs glow with it, empty, low, high, full, warm and colourless, for charge has no element.

Crouch and set a charging crystal on top of the stone and it pours its charge in as fast as the stone takes it, then fills itself again. The chisel can draw from any block of it. Right-click a charged crystal into the stone itself and it stays there, storing charge for the whole line.

And when I strike the stone with the chisel, it takes a verb: it becomes a machine.
journal-livingstone-page4:
One more vessel. Press a block of Awakened sparkstone into an unfired crock on the ground and fire it: a shielded jar. It holds crystals as quietly as the plain one, and I believe it would hold far stronger crystals than any I have grown, safely.

Stronger crystals. I begin to think the stone has more to say, and that not all of it will be kind.
journal-nakedevocations-page1:
Naked Evocations

A charged crystal does more than shine. Hold one in your hand, look at something, and hold right-click. Its note swells over a few slow breaths; let go then, and a streak of its colour leaps to what you looked at and works on it. Let go sooner and nothing happens.

So my hand is for casting now. To set a crystal down I crouch first, as I do with pots. A cradle or a rack still takes one from my hand as before.
journal-nakedevocations-page2:
Each Elemental has its one plain working.

Fire lights what a torch lights, at once: firepits, forges, kilns, torches, and bombs, so mind the bombs. Aimed at ice or snow it melts them instead; at anything else it sets a fire there. Ice puts fire out, as rain does, freezes still fresh water into ice, soaks tilled soil as well as any watering can, and cools lava to stone.
journal-nakedevocations-page3:
Each Elemental, continued.

Earth heaves a square of ground, two blocks by two, two blocks up, and the ground on its four sides sinks to feed it; whoever stands on it rides up too. Only earth and rock will move: if wood, ice or anything built is in the way, or a chest, the note warbles and breaks, and the charge is spent for nothing. Sky throws creatures and dropped things away from me, and its gust strips grown leaves, picks mushrooms, cuts cattails, papyrus and tule as a knife would, so they grow back, and sifts sand and gravel away as a pan would, leaving the finds behind.
journal-nakedevocations-page4:
A small crystal reaches eight blocks and works on one thing. A Glowing one reaches twelve and works on a flat patch three blocks by three around where it strikes: a pillar twice as tall, a patch of ice, and a Glowing Fire sets creatures alight, and people too. My own fire and wind pass over me, and my own Ice puts me out.

Land another has claimed, the stone will not touch, unless they let me build there.
journal-nakedevocations-page5:
It is wasteful. Each working spends a tenth of a full crystal, so ten empty it, and it chimes as it falls each step. With too little left it only clicks dully. A working that finds nothing to act on fizzles in a puff and costs nothing.

Cast from a handful and one crystal pays: it leaves the handful for my pack, so my hand keeps the full ones.
journal-nakedevocations-page6: Hold on, long after it is ready, and the note leaps to a higher key over a rising whine; the crystal flares, and light runs through it like hairline cracks. Let go then and it works as if it were one Evolution higher, a small crystal as a Glowing one, a Glowing one over a cube three blocks across, for twice the charge. One time in three it cracks. The third crack shatters it; a cradle mends the rest.
journal-nakedevocations-page7:
Over-driven, each Elemental does more. A Fire crystal aimed at bare rock melts it into lava, so stand clear, and aimed at water, fresh or salt, it boils a pool of it away and even glacier ice runs; Ice packs lake ice into glacier ice, and glacier ice harder still; and a gust picks ripe crops, berries and fruit, and leaves the bushes and trees standing.

A day to fill and ten breaths to empty. The stone I woke with the chisel learns what it is taught. Taught stone, I think, could do this work for far less.
